info.title: AutoBuy Crypto API
info.description:
Automated cryptocurrency purchasing platform: schedule recurring USDT buys (daily/weekly/biweekly/monthly), executed on Binance with KYC gating, encrypted key storage, and full transaction history.

All protected endpoints expect `Authorization: Bearer <access token>`. Validation failures return **422**; rate limits return **429** with `Retry-After`. Full guides: `docs/API.md`, `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md`.

get.description:
Health check endpoint for monitoring.

``schedulers`` reports the admin pause switch and the Auto-Buy
execute_purchases job from the Redis heartbeat, so the values are the same
whichever worker answers: running / paused, last run time, last result
(``ok`` | ``failed`` | ``error`` | ``skipped_paused``), last counts and the
consecutive-failure count.
Welcome endpoint.

post.description:
Register a new user with email and password. During the private beta
the request must carry the invite code; the refusal is the same whatever
was wrong (missing, mismatched, or no code configured in production), so
it never reveals whether the code or the email was the problem.

Authenticate with email/password. The body carries the short-lived access
token (keep it in memory) and a CSRF token; the refresh token is set as an
httpOnly cookie scoped to /api/auth. An account with two-factor
authentication on gets **202** `{mfa_required, mfa_token, expires_in}`
instead, and finishes at /login/mfa.

202.description: Password accepted; the account has two-factor authentication on. No session yet and no cookies: finish at /login/mfa.

post.description:
Second step of sign-in for an account with two-factor authentication on:
the `mfa_token` from the 202 answer of /login plus either a six-digit
authenticator `code` or one of the account's `recovery_code`s. Answers the
same body and cookies as /login. The token is single-use, lives five
minutes, allows five attempts and dies if the password changes; a wrong
code counts towards the account lockout exactly like a wrong password.

Sign out everywhere: every access and refresh token issued before now
stops working, including the one making this request, and the session
cookies are cleared. Needs a valid bearer token and no CSRF header: a
cross-site page cannot forge the Authorization header.
Verify an access token; returns validity and the user id it belongs to.

Silent session refresh: needs the refresh cookie and the X-CSRF-Token
header matching the CSRF cookie. Answers a new access token and rotates
both cookies (the previous refresh token is revoked). 401 without a valid
cookie, 403 without a valid CSRF header.

Sign out: revoke the refresh token from the cookie server-side and clear
both session cookies. The short-lived access token simply expires. Always
204 once the cookie holds a valid refresh token, **even when the CSRF
header does not match**: the cookies are SameSite=Lax, so a cross-site
POST cannot carry them and a forged sign-out is not possible, while a tab
whose CSRF value went stale after another tab rotated the cookies must
still be able to sign out for real (issue #64). Without a valid refresh
cookie the CSRF check applies as before (there is nothing to revoke).
Change the password and invalidate every token issued before now.

Email a one-hour password reset link. Always answers `{sent: true}`
so the response cannot be used to discover which emails have accounts.

Check a reset token without consuming it: 200 `{valid: true}` when
`/reset-password` would accept it, 400 `{valid: false}` otherwise. Lets
the reset page show the expired-link state before asking for a password.

400.description: Token is invalid, expired or already used

post.description:
Set a new password using a reset token from `/forgot-password`.
The token is single-use and expires after an hour; on success every
existing session is signed out.

get.description:
Supported coins and exchanges, the support address and the server IP to
allowlist on an exchange API key. Anonymous, cacheable for 5 minutes.

Whether two-factor authentication is on for the signed-in account, when
it was enabled, how many recovery codes are unused, and whether an
enrolment is waiting to be confirmed.

post.description:
Start two-factor enrolment: needs the current password and answers a
fresh secret with its otpauth:// URI for the authenticator app. Nothing is
in force until /confirm succeeds. 409 when two-factor is already on (turn
it off first); starting again replaces an unconfirmed enrolment.

Prove the authenticator works and switch two-factor on. Answers the ten
recovery codes, shown this once. 400 when no enrolment is pending or the
code is wrong.

A new set of recovery codes against a current authenticator code (a
recovery code cannot mint more). The previous set stops working.

Turn two-factor off: needs the current password and either an
authenticator code or a recovery code. Refused for admin accounts while
ADMIN_MFA_REQUIRED is on. A wrong password or code counts towards the
account lockout; the account is emailed when it succeeds.

get.description:
Return the authenticated user's own profile, including any active
wallet-change hold (`wallet_hold_until`).

put.description: Update the authenticated user's email and/or KYC status.

get.description: Get any user's public profile by ID (requires authentication).
Exchanges this deployment offers (SUPPORTED_EXCHANGES); keys for others are refused.

schema.title: Response Supported Exchanges Api Exchange Supported Get

get.description: List the authenticated user's API keys (masked).

schema.title: Response List Keys Api Exchange Keys Get

post.description: Add a new API key for an exchange, or update the existing one.

Check the stored key against its exchange with one harmless authenticated
call (account info on Binance/Bitget, a balance read elsewhere) and record
the outcome on the key: verified | failed with a readable reason,
verified_at / last_checked_at, and whether the key can withdraw. Always
200; ``verified`` and ``result`` carry the outcome.

delete.description: Remove one of the authenticated user's API keys.

get.description: List the authenticated user's execution attempts, newest first, paginated.
Aggregate statistics over the user's attempts (invested = successful buys).
List the user's attempts for one cryptocurrency.

schema.title: Response Transactions By Crypto Api Transactions Crypto  Crypto  Get

get.description: List the user's attempts with a given status.

schema.title: Response Transactions By Status Api Transactions Status  Tx Status  Get

get.description: Get one attempt by id.

Main dashboard: holdings, active Auto-Buy purchases (both ``autobuy``
and ``dca`` types), the ones due within 30 days, and the monthly average.
Quick overview numbers for the header/summary widgets.
Daily successful-buy totals for the last `days` days (zero-filled).

Read-only. Portfolio value and amount invested over the range, built from
this customer's successful buys and Bitget candles (see
api/services/portfolio_series.py). 503 when Bitget is unreachable and no
candle page is cached; the rest of the dashboard is unaffected.

503.description: Bitget candles unavailable and nothing cached

get.description: Everything the account can connect, with its current status.

schema.title: Response Available Api Integrations Available Get

get.description: The caller's outbound endpoints (secrets are never returned again).

schema.title: Response List Webhooks Api Integrations Webhooks Get

post.description:
Register an endpoint. The signing secret is returned ONCE — store it;
verify deliveries via X-AutoBuy-Signature (hex HMAC-SHA256 of the body).
Send a signed test event and record the delivery result.

get.description:
FIFO acquisition summary for a calendar year (defaults to the current
one). `format=csv` streams a spreadsheet-ready lot list.

ROI (total and annualized), spend volatility, and buy-cadence facts.
Degrades to cost-basis-only when live prices are unavailable.
PDF acquisition report for the year (accountant-friendly).
The caller's notification channel settings.

put.description:
Update channel toggles, optional email categories (purchase confirmations,
weekly summary, milestones, low-balance warnings), quiet hours (UTC), phone number, device token.
Security and failure emails cannot be switched off.

get.description: Audit log of the caller's notifications across all channels.

post.description: Send a test notification through every enabled channel.

get.description: All users, searchable by email substring, newest first.

post.description: Suspend: blocks login/API access and purchase execution immediately.

Reactivate a suspended account. During the private beta an account that
owns ACTIVE withdraw-mode purchases and isn't allowed withdrawals is refused
(403, the purchase ids listed), because the executor would run them again;
send `{"pause_withdraw_mode": true}` to pause those purchases and reactivate
the account (the owner can switch them to accumulate and resume).

delete.description:
Hard-delete a user and (by cascade) their keys, schedules, and
transactions. `confirm` must match the account email exactly.

post.description:
Support override: clear the 24-hour wallet-change hold for a customer who
reset their own password and proved their identity. Requires the user's
email typed exactly and a reason; writes an audit entry (admin, when, why)
and emails the user that the hold was lifted. 409 when no hold is active.

Manual KYC decision (support escalations). The note is mandatory and
lands in the audit log.

Support path for a lost authenticator: remove the user's two-factor
enrolment and recovery codes so they can sign in with the password alone
and enrol again. Audited; the user is emailed when something was removed.

get.description: Purchases by status (default: the parked ones), with their parked attempts.

Inspect a parked purchase: its attempts and, live from the exchange, what
became of each order (state, fill, and whether the fill would pass the
guard). Read-only. Then POST /resolve.

post.description:
Clear a needs_review purchase after checking the exchange:

- record_fill: the exchange shows the order FILLED and the fill passes the
  guard -> recorded as the buy (never re-bought), schedule resumes, and for
  withdraw-immediately purchases the withdrawal is sent now;
- mark_not_sent: the exchange shows NOT FOUND or CANCELLED -> the attempt is
  marked failed and the purchase is due again (a new buy, after the usual
  reconciliation);
- cancel: stop the purchase; the attempt stays on record.
Every resolution is audited with the admin's note.

Make an Auto-Buy purchase due immediately (the next execute_purchases
run picks it up). A failed purchase is re-armed: status back to active and
the attempt counter reset. Refused for withdrawal_failed / needs_info:
those buys already filled and re-arming would buy again — the owner (or
an admin acting as them) must use retry-withdrawal instead.

get.description: Recent successful buys whose fill deviated beyond FILL_WARN_PCT (newest first).

schema.title: Response Fill Deviations Api Admin Fills Deviations Get

get.description: Platform-wide totals and 7-day trend inputs.

Every user's Auto-Buy execution attempts (purchase_transactions), newest
first; filter by status (pending | completed | failed) and/or user.
What the email outbox could not deliver (and what is still retrying).
Live evaluation of the docs/ALERTING.md conditions (see api/services/admin_alerts.py).

schema.title: Response Alerts Api Admin Alerts Get

post.description:
Emergency stop for BOTH schedulers (legacy recurring tick and the
Auto-Buy execute_purchases job) in every worker. Sets a switch in Redis
that each run checks first; it survives API restarts until resumed.
While paused, runs log that they were skipped and report
``skipped_paused`` in /health.
Clear the pause switch; both schedulers execute again from their next run.

Send one test message to the configured Telegram chat and report the
outcome, so the alert channel can be checked without a real buy.

get.description: Unrealized P&L per holding against live prices.

Average buy price vs the market now, and each coin's share of the
total cost invested.

Spend projection from the user's active Auto-Buy purchases (both
``autobuy`` and ``dca`` types). One-time purchases contribute nothing to
the recurring monthly figure. Estimates only.

30-day daily-return volatility per held or scheduled coin, bucketed
low (< 2%) / moderate (2–5%) / high (>= 5%). A description of the
metric only; no cadence or sizing guidance is produced.

post.description: Create (or reuse) the Sumsub applicant and return a WebSDK token.

get.description:
The caller's KYC status, synced from Sumsub while it is still pending.

Works on localhost without the webhook: while the stored status is
`pending` and an applicant exists, Sumsub is asked for the applicant's
review state and `users.kyc_status` is updated from it. A final stored
status (`verified` / `rejected`) is returned as-is without calling Sumsub
unless `?sync=1` is passed (the page does that after SDK events and on
"Refresh", so a rejected-then-resubmitted applicant can move back to
pending).

parameters.name: sync

schema.description: Force a Sumsub lookup even when the stored status is final
schema.title: Sync

parameters.description: Force a Sumsub lookup even when the stored status is final

post.description:
Sumsub review-result callback. HMAC-verified; updates kyc_status and
notifies the user by email.

Create the caller's Sumsub applicant (legal name + account email) and
remember its id. Idempotent: an account that already has an applicant gets
the existing id back. The email must match the account — KYC identity is
bound to the login, never to an arbitrary address.

get.description:
Live review state for an applicant. Users may only query their own
applicant (admins: any); the caller's kyc_status is synced on the way.

post.description:
Sumsub applicant webhook (applicantReviewed, applicantPending, ...).

The raw body is verified against ``x-payload-digest`` using the algorithm
in ``x-payload-digest-alg`` (default HMAC_SHA256_HEX) before anything is
parsed; every event is logged; review results update the user's
kyc_status through the same path as ``POST /api/kyc/webhook``.

Email the caller a 24-hour verification link for their account address.
The address must be the one on the account.

Send a plain notification email. Users may only notify their own
address; admins may notify any address. The message is sent as text and
HTML-escaped, never rendered as markup.

get.description: All of the caller's Auto-Buy purchases, each with its latest transaction.

schema.title: Response List Purchases Api V2 Purchases Get

post.description:
Create a purchase. `purchase_type` selects the mode: `autobuy` (default:
buy, then withdraw the coins to `wallet_address`, which is required) or
`dca` (buy and accumulate on the exchange; no wallet needed — one may be
given for a later switch). Rejects (422 with `{error, details}`) when a
wallet address does not match the chain's format, is a known burn address,
when Bitget has no online USDT pair for the coin, when the order is below
Bitget's minimum, when the chain is not withdrawable, when the amount after
fees is below Bitget's minimum withdrawal (autobuy), or when the exchange
account is not the caller's.

get.description: One purchase with its full transaction history (newest first).

put.description:
Pause (`status: paused`), resume (`status: active`), change amount/frequency,
or switch mode. Switching to `autobuy` (withdraw immediately) requires
`wallet_address`, `blockchain_network` and `confirm_wallet_address` equal to
the address; the address must be valid, spendable and supported by the
exchange. Cancelled, completed and failed purchases cannot be changed.

delete.description:
Cancel a purchase. The record and its transaction history are kept;
the scheduler will never execute it again.

post.description:
Send the coins of the last filled buy to the wallet again. Only for
purchases parked as `withdrawal_failed` or `needs_info`; the buy is never
repeated. The wallet, chain and Bitget minimum are re-checked first. On
success the purchase becomes `active` again and the schedule resumes; a
failed retry leaves it parked with the new error. Runs in dry-run mode
when AUTOBUY_DRY_RUN is set (nothing is sent).

get.description:
Transaction history for a purchase, optionally filtered by status
(pending / success / failed).

schema.title: Response Purchase Transactions Api V2 Purchases  Purchase Id  Transactions Get

post.description:
Save a wallet. The address must match the declared chain's format
(Bitcoin mainnet, EVM 0x…, Solana, Tron); addresses are unique platform-wide.

get.description: The caller's wallets, newest first; filter with `?blockchain_network=BTC|ERC20|...`.

schema.title: Response List Wallets Api Wallets Get

delete.description: Remove a saved wallet. Existing purchases keep their address.

get.description:
Bitget pair + withdrawal chains for a coin; with `amount_usd`, each chain
also reports the fee in USD, what the wallet would receive and whether the
amount clears the minimum withdrawal.

Validate an address (+ destination type + memo) for a chain with the same
rule the purchase and wallet endpoints enforce, and on tag chains ask the
public ledger whether the account exists (a never-funded address is a
warning, not a refusal: Bitget's minimums exceed both reserves).

ActivePurchase.title: ActivePurchase
ActivePurchase.description:
An active Auto-Buy purchase (either type). Field names are kept from the
original schedule shape so existing clients keep working: ``crypto`` is
the purchase's crypto_symbol, ``amount_usdt`` its amount_usd and
``next_purchase_date`` its next_execution.

note.title: Note
note.default: Fees and minimums are Bitget's live values, cached for up to an hour.

ComparisonResponse.title: ComparisonResponse
ComparisonResponse.description:
Average buy price vs the market, and each coin's share of invested
cost. No score is derived from the shares: the shares are the fact.

CryptoHolding.title: CryptoHolding
CryptoHolding.description:
What the customer owns of a coin and where it is. total_amount is the
quantity ACQUIRED (net of the trading fee charged in the coin); on_exchange
is what is still on Bitget after real withdrawals (matches Bitget's balance);
sent_to_wallet is what those withdrawals delivered.

DestinationCheckOut.title: DestinationCheckOut
DestinationCheckOut.description: Server-side verdict on a withdrawal destination before the form submits.

EnrolResponse.title: EnrolResponse
EnrolResponse.description: Shown once. The secret never comes back from the API again.

MfaRequiredResponse.title: MfaRequiredResponse
MfaRequiredResponse.description:
The password was accepted but the account has two-factor authentication
on. No session is issued and no cookie is set: exchange `mfa_token` plus a
code at /login/mfa within `expires_in` seconds.

PerformanceResponse.title: PerformanceResponse
PerformanceResponse.description:
Per-holding figures only. No ranking (best/worst) is produced: every
percentage is in the table and ordering them adds judgement, not fact.

PortfolioSeriesResponse.title: PortfolioSeriesResponse
PortfolioSeriesResponse.description:
Portfolio value over a range: history from Bitget candle closes, the last
point at the same current price the performance card uses. A bucket with
no candle carries the previous close forward (carried_forward counts them).

RecoveryCodesResponse.title: RecoveryCodesResponse
RecoveryCodesResponse.description: Shown once; the previous codes stop working.

note.title: Note
note.default: Estimates only, not financial advice; past performance doesn't guarantee future results.

TokenResponse.title: TokenResponse
TokenResponse.description:
The access token is returned in the body and must be kept in memory only.
The refresh token never appears in a body: it travels in an httpOnly cookie
scoped to /api/auth, and `csrf_token` (also set as a readable cookie) must
be echoed in the X-CSRF-Token header on /refresh and /logout.

TransactionResponse.title: TransactionResponse
TransactionResponse.description:
One execution attempt. ``cost_usdt``/``exchange_rate``/``binance_order_id``
keep their historical names for existing clients; ``order_id`` and the
withdrawal fields are the new, explicit ones.

TravelRuleInfo.title: TravelRuleInfo
TravelRuleInfo.description:
Optional beneficiary / travel-rule details some venues require before an
API withdrawal (Bitget: firstName, lastName, identityType, companyName,
areaCode, memberCode). Stored on the purchase and sent with withdrawals.
Nothing is prefilled: the KYC provider's data is not stored on the user.
